message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) | Dominated by the most abundant isotope, protium (¹H). |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium, 99.98 %), ²H (deuterium, 0.02 %), ³H (tritium, trace, radioactive). | Deuterium and tritium are used in nuclear fusion research. |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron; forms covalent bonds. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among all elements, making H highly electronegative. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Highest of all elements, reflecting strong attraction to its lone electron. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | Negative value indicates energy release when H gains an electron. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; hydrogen is a gas at room temperature. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Solidifies only at cryogenic temperatures. |
| **Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | Very light; lighter than air. |
| **Molar volume (ideal gas, 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | Standard reference for gas calculations. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals. | Forms H₂O, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| **Bonding** | Typically forms single covalent bonds (H–H, H–C, H–O). | Can also form ionic bonds as H⁺ (proton) or H⁻ (hydride). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series in UV/visible/IR. | Classic example of hydrogen atom’s spectral lines. |
| **Molecular form** | H₂ (diatomic) | Most common stable form under normal conditions. |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (as H⁺), –1 (as H⁻), 0 (as H₂). | Determines its role in acids, bases, and redox reactions. |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (H⁺ donor) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺). | In organic chemistry, behaves as a hydrogen atom (neutral). |
| **Solubility** | Poor in water (~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 20 °C) | Solubility increases slightly with pressure. |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive mixture with air (4–75 % H₂). | Requires careful handling. |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), metallurgy (reducing agent), chemical synthesis (hydrogenation), space propulsion, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents). | Also used in isotope separation and nuclear fusion research. |

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Atomic number 1, lowest mass, very low density.
- **Highly reactive**: Strongly electronegative, high ionization energy, forms a wide variety of compounds.
- **Gas at room temperature**: Boiling and melting points far below ambient conditions.
- **Key roles**: Energy carrier (fuel cells), reducing agent in metallurgy, building block in organic chemistry, and a cornerstone of astrophysics and cosmology (first element formed after the Big Bang).

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
